summary.name: NTFSTool
summary.one_liner: NTFSTool is a Mac utility that mounts Windows NTFS drives with full read and write access without a kernel extension, offered as a free Mac App Store edition and a paid one-time Pro version.
keywords: write to ntfs drive on mac
use_cases: Read and write an external Windows NTFS drive on a Mac
Repair a drive Windows left dirty or hibernated
Unlock and use a BitLocker-encrypted drive on a Mac
Format a drive as NTFS from macOS
Check disk health and speed of a USB drive
Avoid lowering Mac security settings for NTFS access
summary.what_it_does: NTFSTool mounts NTFS drives automatically with full read and write access when plugged into a Mac, without a kernel extension or Recovery Mode. It offers a free edition on the Mac App Store and a paid NTFSTool Pro with one-time pricing. Pro adds BitLocker unlocking, instant file name search, in-file content search, and support for NTFS, BitLocker, exFAT, FAT32, HFS+ and APFS formats. Other tools include One-click First Aid repair, NTFS erase, S.M.A.R.T. health status, a speed test, and per-drive settings such as read-only mode. The page also describes an optional Apple FSKit-based driver with fallback to the default driver.
notable: No kernel extension and no lowered Mac security settings, unlike Paragon NTFS and Tuxera per the page
Open-source project with 4,000+ GitHub stars, listed in awesome-mac
Pro is a one-time purchase (US$24.99 per page) with a 45-day read/write guarantee
Includes BitLocker read/write and file content search in Pro
caveats: Free Mac App Store edition requires macOS 15.6 or later; Pro requires macOS 12 or later, and macOS 10.15–11 get a classic version
Full read/write features and BitLocker support are in the paid Pro edition
Competitor comparison and speed figures are the vendor's own measurements as of October 2026
